about: The public surface of a public OpenPlans instance in one file: the /status.json keys, the MCP tools an anonymous caller sees, the keys every /v1/data-availability row carries, the link-outs an unknown answer may carry, and the error shape. The tests and the deployment checks read this file. Changing it needs a note in changes/unreleased/ that names docs/public-contract.json.

usage_report.note: The opt-in usage report stays off on a public instance. Older images do not serve the key.

optional_on: MCP check_drug_coverage, check_provider_network and quote cells
links.note: Pages a person can open; OpenPlans never fetches them. REST items also carry source_row; MCP items carry https URLs only.

reasons.rule: Every unknown status says why: a reason beside it, drawn from this list. Lower snake case.

readiness.note: A ready /readyz answer, and a /healthz answer that is healthy and not waiting for migrations, carry these fields. A 503 answer never does. release is the package version read once at startup; generation and pricing are the ids a release check compares across slots, null when unreadable; plan_years is the served window; schema counts applied migration files, null when the process runs no migration check.

request_id.note: Every API and MCP HTTP response carries the header. A client-sent value of 1 to 128 visible ASCII characters is echoed; anything else is replaced with a generated 16 hex digit id. Every REST error body carries the same value as error.request_id.

rest.note: Every REST route family answers with this one body, the compatibility routes included. Codes are lower snake case. A route may add typed members such as plan_id or year beside these. error.request_id repeats the x-request-id response header (see request_id).
